The '''2016–17 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] during the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]].  The [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|Bruins]] were led by fourth-year head coach [[Steve Alford]] and played their home games at [[Pauley Pavilion]] as members in the [[Pac-12 Conference]]. They rode their offense to a 28–3 regular season record, averaging 91 points per game with a 53 percent [[field goal percentage]].<ref name=kaufman_03102017>{{cite news|last=Kaufman |first=Joey |title=UCLA falls in Pac-12 Tournament semifinals to Arizona |date=March 10, 2017 |newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News |url=http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20170310/ucla-falls-in-pac-12-tournament-semifinals-to-arizona |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170312084008/http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20170310/ucla-falls-in-pac-12-tournament-semifinals-to-arizona |archive-date=March 12, 2017 |url-status=live }}</ref> The talented squad featured five future players in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), including three eventual first-round [[NBA draft|draft picks]].<ref name=phillips_12292018>{{cite news|last=Phillips|first=Ryan|title=UCLA Needs To Fire Steve Alford|date=December 29, 2018|work=The Big Lead|publisher=USA Today|url=https://thebiglead.com/2018/12/29/steve-alford-ucla-fired/|access-date=January 3, 2019}}</ref>

UCLA entered the season ranked No. 16 in the preseason. After starting 13–0, the first time they were undefeated in non-conference play since they won a national championship in [[1994–95 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|1994–95]], they moved up to No. 2 in the country.<ref>{{cite news|last=Bolch |first=Ben |title=Bruins to open Pac-12 play with 'target on our back' |date=December 27, 2016 |newspaper=The Los Angeles Times |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-basketball-20161227-story.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170101091700/http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-basketball-20161227-story.html |archive-date=January 1, 2017 |url-status=live }}</ref> However, the Bruins suffered their first defeat in an 89–87 loss to No. 21 [[2016–17 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Oregon]] in the conference opener.<ref>{{cite news|last=Bolch |first=Ben |title=Second-ranked UCLA takes a harsh shot, losing in final second to No. 21 Oregon |date=December 28, 2016 |newspaper=The Los Angeles Times |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-oregon-20161228-story.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170101091748/http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-oregon-20161228-story.html |archive-date=January 1, 2017 |url-status=live }}</ref> UCLA won their next six games before losing at home to No. 14 [[2016–17 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]] for their first loss of the season at Pauley Pavilion. The Wildcats exposed the Bruins weaknesses on defense, which had to that point been obscured by their potent offense.<ref>{{cite news|last=Bolch |first=Ben |title=UCLA has little to celebrate (except Kareem) during 96-85 loss to Arizona |date=January 21, 2017 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-arizona-20170121-story.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170122200738/http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-arizona-20170121-story.html |archive-date=January 22, 2017 |url-status=live }}</ref> They suffered their second consecutive defeat after falling to [[2016–17 USC Trojans men's basketball team|USC]], who won for the fourth straight time in [[UCLA–USC rivalry|their crosstown rivalry]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Bolch |first=Ben |title=UCLA holds a lengthy team meeting after fourth consecutive loss to USC |date=January 26, 2017 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-folo-20170126-story.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170131011539/http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-folo-20170126-story.html |archive-date=January 31, 2017 |url-status=live }}</ref> They won their last nine games of the regular season to tie the school record for most regular season wins.<ref>{{cite news|last=Fowler |first=Clay |title=Will UCLA's offensive philosophy stand up in tournament play? |date=March 8, 2017 |newspaper=The Orange County Register |url=http://www.ocregister.com/articles/team-746063-ucla-offensive.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170310103736/http://www.ocregister.com/articles/team-746063-ucla-offensive.html |archive-date=March 10, 2017 |url-status=live }}</ref>

The Bruins struggled uncharacteristically with their offense during the  [[2017 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 tournament]]. They beat USC 76–74 while shooting just 41.2 percent before shooting a season-low 40.7 percent in an 86–75 loss to Arizona in the semifinals.<ref name=kaufman_03102017/> UCLA entered the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as a third seed in the South region. They advanced to the Sweet Sixteen for the third time in four years, where they lost 86–75 to [[2016-17 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]].

==Previous season==
{{main|2015–16 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team}}

The Bruins finished the season 15–17 overall; and 6–12 in the conference. During the season, the Bruins were invited and participated in the [[2015 Maui Invitational Tournament|Maui Invitational]] in [[Maui, Hawaii]]. UCLA defeated [[2015–16 Cal Poly Mustangs men's basketball team|Cal Poly]] and [[2015–16 UNLV Runnin' Rebels men's basketball team|UNLV]] but lost against [[2015–16 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]] and [[2015–16 Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball team|Wake Forest]] to earn 4th place. UCLA also lost to [[2015–16 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] in the [[CBS Sports Classic]] in [[Brooklyn, New York]]. In the postseason, the Bruins lost to [[2015–16 USC Trojans men's basketball team|USC]] in the first round of the [[2016 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament]] in [[Paradise, Nevada]].
